proposals.expected_failure_mode: If admissions track a distinct hospitalized process rather than a lagged infectious proxy, delayed_I may mis-time the peak and under/over-shoot shoulders.
proposals.rationale: Hospitalization-rate target can plausibly lag the infectious proxy; SEIRS supports moderate peakiness with potential short-term immunity waning, and a 2-week delay matches the stated surveillance semantics while staying parsimonious.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: H compartment may be weakly identifiable in a short series, leading to unstable separation of I vs H dynamics and overfitting of admission timing.
proposals.rationale: Directly maps the target to an explicit hospitalized compartment, aligning with hospitalization-rate semantics; SEIHR can capture decoupling between infections and admissions without requiring an ad hoc delay.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the target is strictly admissions (not mixed burden), I+H can bias level/shape and inflate persistence after the peak.
proposals.rationale: If reported hospitalization rates reflect a mixture of current infectious burden and admissions/occupancy effects, observing I+H can be a robust compromise that reduces identifiability pressure on H alone.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Extra flexibility from fractional dynamics can mimic noise and distort extrapolation, especially if the true lag is longer than 1 week.
proposals.rationale: Fractional SEIRS can flexibly represent heterogeneous contact/recovery processes in high-rate pediatric series; a 1-week delay accommodates short reporting/admission lag while remaining simple.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If immunity waning or multi-wave behavior matters, SEIR may underfit late-season rebounds; 3-week delay can over-shift peaks and degrade short-horizon timing.
proposals.rationale: A simpler non-waning immunity model may suffice over a single season; a longer (3-week) delay tests the upper plausible lag between infection proxy and hospitalization reporting.
